currentUse: The former St. Francis church at the foot of Saint Francis Street in Minersville remains standing, but the Diocese of Allentown closed the underused church building effective with the July 1, 2020 Minersville merger. Before that closure the building had been used only for one annual Mass on the feast of St. Francis and for funerals, with no funeral there since 2008. Its present reuse, access, and disposition are unresolved. Holy Family Parish of Minersville is the current local successor context, but neither it nor hosted annual worship should be conflated with the former Lithuanian parish institution.
summary: St. Francis of Assisi was Minersville's Lithuanian Roman Catholic parish. Successor-parish and secondary histories place its establishment in 1895, and contemporary Draugas pages document dedication of a new Lithuanian St. Francis church on November 25, 1909. The parish school was staffed by the Sisters of St. Casimir and the parish remained a source of Lithuanian religious vocations. By 1972 its longtime pastor said Lithuanian-language activity had ended after World War II even as younger, increasingly non-Lithuanian membership kept the parish active. The Diocese suppressed St. Francis into St. Matthew the Evangelist in July 2008. A canonical appeal concerned the church building, not restoration of the parish; the reviewed record does not support claims of a Minersville civil-court victory. Limited annual worship continued in the building until it closed in the July 1, 2020 formation of Holy Family Parish of Minersville. The juridic parish end and the building closure are separate events.

historicalNarrative.text: St. Francis was organized for Minersville's Lithuanian Roman Catholics. Later parish histories place the institution's establishment in 1895; contemporary newspaper evidence independently proves the parish by 1909. Draugas invitations and a dedication report record that a new Lithuanian St. Francis church was dedicated on November 25, 1909. The 1950 date once attached to the record is not a founding date and is superseded by the 1895 reading and the 1909 contemporary evidence.

historicalNarrative.text: The parish complex included a school on the hill above the church, staffed by the Sisters of St. Casimir. Minersville daughters entered the congregation from St. Francis during the 1920s and 1930s, and Sister M. Lydia Antanaitis later served five years as school principal. In the 1960s Father Alfonsas Babonas served Minersville after New Philadelphia and Easton, showing that Lithuanian clergy links remained active well beyond the immigrant generation.

historicalNarrative.text: A 1972 interview with longtime pastor Monsignor J. Klevinskas-Klevence described a parish changing ethnic composition. He said Lithuanian choir and organized activity had ended with World War II, but opening membership to non-Lithuanians brought many younger people; he also recalled burying about one thousand Lithuanians in the parish cemetery. By December 2007 Draugas itself wrote of the church in the past tense and admitted it lacked current knowledge, even though the parish had not yet been suppressed. This gap cautions against using the newspaper's silence as closure evidence.

sources.locator: Draugas, 2007-12-01, pp. 14–15: Petras Petrutis retrospective and quoted 1972 Klevinskas-Klevence interview

historicalNarrative.text: The Diocese suppressed St. Francis into St. Matthew the Evangelist in July 2008. Parishioners pursued canonical recourse concerning closure of the church building; the resulting Allentown rulings did not restore the suppressed parish, and the available evidence does not establish that St. Francis won a civil lawsuit. The church later opened only for one annual St. Francis feast Mass and funerals. In June 2020 parish committees unanimously recommended closing the underused building, and the action accompanied the July 1 merger of St. Matthew and St. Michael into Holy Family Parish of Minersville. The relationships are suppression into St. Matthew, then successor-context consolidation into Holy Family, with the St. Francis building separately closed in 2020.

conflictsWithArchiveRecord: The 1895 establishment reading supersedes a 1950 founding interpretation; contemporary Draugas evidence proves the parish by 1909. Institution life, building life, and hosted worship are separate: the parish was suppressed into St. Matthew in July 2008, annual Mass and funeral use continued in the former church, and the building closed effective 2020-07-01. The popular civil-court-victory narrative conflates St. Francis's canonical appeal with St. George Shenandoah's separate civil litigation. Draugas did not report the St. Francis closure case and cannot be cited as proof of it.
gaps: The original 1895 erection instrument, exact street-number history, complete church-building chronology before 1909, the suppression decree's exact effective day, the St. Francis-specific canonical-recoursing documents and result, sacramental-record custody, and the standing building's post-2020 owner, access, repair condition, and reuse remain unresolved.
